brief: THE BET. Twenty iterations built the night and a visitor landing at noon never sees it: the day is 55 s, dusk is ~35 s away, and the only fast-forward is the season button, which skips a quarter-YEAR. Make the sill's clock (`#daytime`) a button too: a tap takes the town to this evening — the same `beginSkip`/`simSub`/`skipEase` lapse the season button uses (SKIP_SUB-bounded, so the argument that no step is too long still holds), aimed at `sunDown + ~1 h` of the current day instead of a season boundary, over 2–3 real seconds behind the same veil in RM. Tap again at night → the next dawn. It joins `OFFERS` as the next invitation and does not get a hint of its own. Prove the lapse leaves the town honest: window hours and homers behave as if the evening arrived at 1x (`windows-night.mjs` lit counts within the usual spread of a 1x run to the same instant), agents mid-route are where a 1x run would put them, `stepWind`/`stepWet`/`cloudCover` are continuous across it, and the night filmstrip after a tap reads 0 POP.
successLooksLike: A fresh page at noon, one tap on the clock, and 3 s later it is a lamp-lit evening with the door open and the river lamps on; a second tap and it is morning; `season-skip.mjs` still passes for the season button; `naming.mjs` all pass; phone 390px layout unchanged; the follow line (c98) is released or preserved deliberately — say which and why.
avoid: Do not build a second lapse mechanism — extend the one that exists with a different target. Do not let the two buttons run at once. Do not make the ticker carry a hint for it.
